$comment: The wide-net channel: a bit of everything, chosen for viral potential rather than for a niche. This is the only channel with real subscribers, so it is the one where a bad video costs something.

channel.name: MyMixVault
channel.niche: Anything with a genuinely surprising fact at the centre of it — no fixed subject, chosen for how hard it is to scroll past
channel.audience: 16-30, English-speaking, broad general audience with no particular interest in common beyond wanting to be told something they did not know
channel.promise: One fact you will want to repeat to someone, in under 30 seconds

voice.persona: The friend who opens with 'okay, this is going to sound made up' and then turns out to be right.
do: Lead with the most surprising part — no setup, no context first
Keep it under 30 seconds; this channel lives on completion rate
Make the fact repeatable — the viewer should be able to retell it
Land on something that invites a comment, not a subscribe request
dont: No 'you won't believe', 'wait for it', 'watch till the end' — earn it instead
No unverified facts. A wrong fact on this channel is worse than a boring one, because the comments will do the correcting

cadence.$comment: Highest volume of the four — a wide-net channel needs shots on goal, and each video is short.

compliance.affiliateDisclosure: #ad — affiliate link. I earn a commission if you join.

sources.$comment: Anything goes, as long as the fact is true and checkable. Put the surprising part in angleNotes — that is what the hook gets built from.

topics.$comment: REPLACE ME. The angleNotes field is the video; the title is just a label.
topics.title: Example: the reason lobsters were once prison food
topics.angleNotes: Replace this entry. Write the single surprising fact, and where you verified it.
